mfrmr Reports and Tables Map

Source: R/help_reports_and_tables.R
mfrmr_reports_and_tables.Rd

Quick guide to choosing the right report or table helper in mfrmr. Use this page when you know the reporting question but have not yet decided which bundle, table, or reporting helper to call.

Recommended report route

For ordinary MML/JML mfrm_fit results, start here. The Examples section follows the same route with bundled data.

  1. Inspect summary(fit)$decision before interpreting the estimates.

  2. Collect res <- mfrm_results(fit). By default it computes missing requested diagnostics. Pass existing matching checks through diagnostics = diagnostics to reuse them; compute = "never" leaves missing diagnostics unavailable. Saved intervals are explicit attachments.

  3. Read summary(res)$triage and $next_actions; use $plot_map to find supported figures. A failed or unavailable component needs its own explanation, not an automatically substituted analysis.

  4. Choose mfrm_report(res) for an analyst report, plot(res, ...) for a supported figure, or export_mfrm_results() for tables and an archive. Save the complete object with saveRDS(res, file) for later R use. Reopen with readRDS(file); reading or displaying saved outputs does not refit the model. Reports and figures are optional, not required to save.

Native CML and comparison-only fits do not supply ordinary consolidated reports. Read summary(fit); for CML use mfrm_facet_intervals(), then summary(ci), plot(ci), apa_table() and saveRDS(ci, file). G/D-study and observed-agreement results also have their own summary and saving routes. For GPCM or extended measurement models, mfrm_results() states the supported sections and attachments; model-specific uncertainty limits remain in the collected results.

Individual helpers below answer additional questions. build_apa_outputs() drafts manuscript text; build_summary_table_bundle() collects selected tables for export_summary_appendix(). Neither is a prerequisite for mfrm_report(). Use mfrmr_output_guide("beginner") for a compact question-to-function map, or the full guide for specialist routes.

Choose what to save

  • export_mfrm_tables(): core CSV tables from a fitted model. Supplied matching diagnostics enrich the tables; this call does not compute them.

  • export_mfrm_results(): selected tables/reports and, by default, the complete results RDS plus a script that reloads it without refitting.

  • export_mfrm_bundle(): fit-level tables, optional diagnostics and a refitting recipe. Its "script" component reruns the analysis; it does not preserve a fitted R object. Supply the original data for a colocated replay CSV, or replace the script's data-path placeholder yourself.

  • export_summary_appendix(): selected summary tables for a manuscript. Display rounding follows digits; retain the source R object for reuse.

No export certifies estimates as usable or changes their uncertainty target. Inspect availability and caveat fields along with estimates. For G/D-study or native CML objects, use saveRDS() for the complete object and write.csv() for a selected supported summary table; the MFRM exporters do not widen their accepted model classes.

Start with the question

  • "How can I read assessment-plan estimates and uncertainty together?" Use summary.mfrm_multivariate_d_study() with intervals = TRUE and assumption = "normal", or supply saved intervals. Its table, intervals and notes retain methods, design and interpretation limits.

  • "How should I document the model setup and run settings?" Use specifications_report().

  • "Was data filtered, dropped, or mapped in unexpected ways?" Use data_quality_report() and describe_mfrm_data().

  • "Did estimation converge cleanly and how formal is the precision layer?" Use estimation_iteration_report() and precision_review_report().

  • "Which facets are measurable, variable, or weakly separated?" Use facet_statistics_report(), measurable_summary_table(), and facets_chisq_table().

  • "Are score categories functioning in a usable sequence?" Use rating_scale_table(), category_structure_report(), and category_curves_report().

  • "Is the design linked well enough across subsets, forms, or waves?" Use subset_connectivity_report() and plot(x).

  • "What should go into the manuscript text and tables?" For ordinary MML/JML RSM / PCM, use reporting_checklist(), build_apa_outputs(), and build_summary_table_bundle() or export_summary_appendix(). For GPCM, use the same route only where gpcm_capability_matrix() marks it as supported_with_caveat: direct table/plot helpers, summary-table appendix export, caveated build_apa_outputs(), and caveated export_mfrm_bundle() are available with a gpcm_boundary; score-side exports and design-forecasting evidence use their own caveated or blocked GPCM routes.

  • "How can I estimate my model in Stan or brms?" export_mfrm_model() writes code, data, mappings and explicit Bayesian priors for supported ordinary MML specifications. Export does not run a sampler; posterior credible intervals are distinct from MML intervals. After sampling, use read_mfrm_posterior() to read the saved summary, inspect its sampling review, and continue with plot(), confint() and mfrm_report(). The summary does not contain joint posterior draws.

  • "Did a simulation recover the known generating parameters well enough?" Use simulate_mfrm_recovery() for the recovery study, assess_mfrm_recovery() for the adequacy checklist, and then build_summary_table_bundle() or export_summary_appendix() for the appendix handoff.

Which output answers which question

specifications_report()

Documents model type, estimation method, anchors, and core run settings. Best for method sections and reproducibility records.

data_quality_report()

Summarizes retained and dropped rows, missingness, and unknown elements. Best for data cleaning narratives.

estimation_iteration_report()

Shows replayed convergence trajectories. Best for diagnosing slow or unstable estimation.

precision_review_report()

Summarizes whether SE, CI, and reliability indices are model-based, hybrid, or exploratory. Best for deciding how strongly to phrase inferential claims.

facet_statistics_report()

Bundles facet summaries, precision summaries, and variability tests. Best for facet-level reporting.

subset_connectivity_report()

Summarizes disconnected subsets and coverage bottlenecks. Best for linking and anchor strategy review.

rating_scale_table()

Gives category counts, average measures, and threshold diagnostics. Best for first-pass category evaluation.

category_structure_report()

Adds transition points and compact category warnings. Best for category-order interpretation.

category_curves_report()

Returns category-probability, cumulative-probability, expected-ogive, total-information, and category-specific information coordinates. Best for downstream graphics and report drafts.

write_mfrm_residual_file()

Writes an observation-level residual file, optionally with modeled category probabilities. Best for external case review or reproducible handoff.

write_mfrm_subset_file()

Writes connected-subset summary and node-membership files. Best for scale-linking review outside R.

reporting_checklist()

Turns analysis status into an action list with priorities and next steps. Best for closing reporting gaps.

build_apa_outputs()

Creates manuscript-draft text, notes, captions, and section maps from a shared reporting contract.

build_summary_table_bundle()

Converts supported summary() outputs into named data.frame tables with a compact index for appendix or manuscript handoff, including recovery simulation and recovery assessment outputs. It also supports bundle-level summary() / plot() for QC before export.

export_summary_appendix()

Exports those documented summary-table bundles as CSV and optional HTML appendix artifacts without requiring the broader fit-based export bundle. This is the preferred export route for recovery simulation evidence.

apa_table()

Can now take those summary-table bundles directly, so a selected component can move from summary() to a formatted handoff table without rebuilding the analysis object path.

Read availability and method limits separately

An available table or a passed numerical check does not establish that its intervals have accurate repeated-sample coverage. For implemented experimental methods, incomplete qualification means that a stated statistical property remains unestablished; inspect the specific limitation before interpreting it. Corrected JML retains this explanation in interpretation_notes, two-family GPCM in gpcm_interpretation_notes, and attached population intervals in population_<name>_interpretation_notes. These tables accompany the other result tables in reports and CSV exports; keep them with the estimates.

An IntervalStatus of Incomplete has a different meaning: only one endpoint was computed. It is neither an infinite bound nor a qualified one-sided interval. Unavailable means the requested result was not supplied; inspect its reason. CIEligible, where present, concerns that interval procedure's checks, not a universal coverage guarantee. Keep numerical status, method limitations and unavailable results when saving or sharing an analysis.

Practical interpretation rules

  • Use bundle summaries first, then drill down into component tables.

  • Use precision_review_report() to determine whether formal inference is supported for the fitted result.

  • Treat category and bias outputs as complementary layers rather than substitutes for overall fit review.

  • Treat zero-count score categories as scale-functioning caveats. Boundary zero-count categories can be retained with explicit rating_min / rating_max; retaining an intermediate zero-count category with keep_original = TRUE creates an unsupported adjacent-step contrast in a polytomous fitted ladder, so new fits stop before optimization. summary(describe_mfrm_data(...)) exposes these in Notes, printed Caveats, and $caveats; summary(fit) carries full structured caveats into printed Caveats and $caveats, with Key warnings as a short triage subset. Summary-table exports use score_category_caveats and analysis_caveats.

  • Use reporting_checklist() before build_apa_outputs() when a report still needs missing diagnostics or clearer caveats.

Additional task-specific workflows

These extend the basic route for eligible ordinary fits; they are not extra steps required for every report and do not apply to native CML.

  • Run documentation: fit_mfrm() -> specifications_report() -> data_quality_report().

  • Precision and facet review: diagnose_mfrm() -> precision_review_report() -> facet_statistics_report().

  • Scale review: rating_scale_table() -> category_structure_report() -> category_curves_report().

  • Manuscript handoff (RSM / PCM): reporting_checklist() -> build_apa_outputs() -> build_summary_table_bundle() -> summary() / plot() -> apa_table() or export_summary_appendix() / export_mfrm_bundle()(include = "summary_tables").

  • GPCM handoff: reporting_checklist() -> direct summaries/plots -> build_apa_outputs() or build_summary_table_bundle() -> export_summary_appendix() or caveated export_mfrm_bundle(), with gpcm_boundary retained in report/export objects.

  • Recovery simulation handoff: simulate_mfrm_recovery() -> plot() / assess_mfrm_recovery() -> build_summary_table_bundle() -> export_summary_appendix().

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrmr_reports_and_tables", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the package and example ratings
library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")

# Fit the model
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

summary(fit)$decision # Review the fit before interpreting it

# Build the comprehensive results and report
res <- mfrm_results(fit)
report <- mfrm_report(res)
summary(report, view = "reader")

# Find report sections that need attention
report$first_screen[, c("Area", "Status", "MainIssue", "NextAction")]

# Extract individual person, rater, and criterion estimates
estimates <- as.data.frame(fit)
head(subset(estimates, Facet == "Person")) # First six persons
subset(estimates, Facet == "Rater")       # All raters
subset(estimates, Facet == "Criterion")   # All criteria

# Keep the full result, including methods and unavailable-output reasons
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # Choose a lasting path for your analysis
saveRDS(res, file)
saved <- readRDS(file)
summary(saved)$triage # No refitting or repeated diagnostic calculation
} # }
